name: Gingival Fibromatosis-Progressive Deafness Syndrome
aliases: Gingival Fibromatosis with Progressive Sensorineural Deafness

criteria.description: Presence of progressive gingival fibromatosis characterized by firm, fibrous gingival overgrowth
Bilateral progressive sensorineural deafness typically manifesting in childhood or adolescence
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both gingival fibromatosis and progressive sensorineural hearing loss
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always available.

imaging: Audiometry confirming bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
CT or MRI may be normal or show no specific abnormalities
genetic: Mutations in the SOS1 gene reported in some families
other: Histopathology of gingival tissue shows dense fibrous connective tissue proliferation without inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Gingival fibromatosis without associated hearing loss
Sensorineural hearing loss with retinitis pigmentosa
Gingival fibromatosis with nail and skeletal abnormalities
Facial dysmorphism distinct from GF-PD syndrome

redFlags: Rapid progression of hearing loss in childhood
Severe gingival overgrowth causing airway obstruction
Family history of similar symptoms indicating inherited disorder
references: Smith RJH, et al. Progressive sensorineural hearing loss associated with gingival fibromatosis. Am J Med Genet. 1994.
